column1: # deny-corpus.tsv: the cases bin/test-deny-rules replays against the Bash
# deny rules in settings.json, one per line:
# right is the right answer: deny when the command runs git commit, push, merge
# or pull with the git hooks off, or switches them off; allow otherwise. It is
# not what the rules happen to do. measured is the answer Claude Code's own
# matcher gave when the row was last probed live: deny when a rule refused it,
# allow when it ran. A rule change is probed again only on the rows whose
# verdict it moves, so the other rows keep their last measured answer. A row
# whose two answers differ is a known gap, and its why says so.
# In the command, \n is a newline, \t a tab and \\ a backslash (no other

# escapes), and

stands for the scratch repository the probes ran in.
